dedupe_keys.name: qsdsan quantitative sustainable design for sanitation and resource recovery systems

description: QSDsan is an open-source, community-led Python platform for the quantitative sustainable design of sanitation and resource recovery systems. It integrates process modelling, system simulation, techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment, builds on the BioSTEAM platform, and ships built-in unit operations and systems, including common treatment processes and biokinetic models, to compare treatment configurations and weigh energy, cost and sustainability trade-offs of emerging technologies. The Quantitative Sustainable Design Group produced and maintains it; version 1.5.3 was released on PyPI in June 2026 and the documentation covers 1.6.0. It is free to install with pip under the University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License, with source on GitHub and tutorials on Read the Docs. Coverage is global in the sense that it is not tied to a place; users supply local data. Caveats: it models treatment plants and sanitation chains, not pipe networks, it needs Python 3.12 or later, and Graphviz for diagrams. Simulation uses: comparing and sizing wastewater and sanitation treatment options for capacity planning and cost or impact optimisation. Related records: the EPA non-potable water reuse calculator (model-epa-newr-non-potable-water-reuse-calculator) and wastewater unit process removal and cost data (data-wastewater-treatment-unit-processes-removal-costs).
